important.name: Workflow-args mirror pins constants the parser never reads
important.summary: matrixRow.ts declares WORKFLOW_ARG_KEYS ('run_key', 'run_id') and WORKFLOW_SLOT_KEYS ('id', 'model') as the keys the mod reads (doc comment at :86-88), and tests/mods/test_agent_watcher_adversarial_mirror.py pins them to review_adversarial.workflow_args, its docstring claiming it 'fails when either side changes without the other'. But neither constant is referenced anywhere: matchedKey reads a.run_key / a.run_id literally (:123-124), workflowPlan reads a.reviewers and a.run_id literally (:136, :138), and groupSlots reads e.id / e.model literally (:114-115). Only WORKFLOW_GROUPS / WORKFLOW_ROLES feed the code (:137). A rename in workflow_args that is mirrored by updating the TS constants passes the pin test while workflowPlan keeps reading the old keys and silently logs no Workflow rows: exactly the drift EX11 added the test to stop.
fix: Make the parser read through the pinned constants: destructure `const [RUN_KEY, RUN_ID] = WORKFLOW_ARG_KEYS` and `const [SLOT_ID, SLOT_MODEL] = WORKFLOW_SLOT_KEYS`, then use a[RUN_KEY], a[RUN_ID], a[WORKFLOW_GROUPS[0]] and e[SLOT_ID], e[SLOT_MODEL] in matchedKey, workflowPlan and groupSlots, so the pinned list is the list read.
Or drop WORKFLOW_ARG_KEYS / WORKFLOW_SLOT_KEYS and have the mirror test parse the literal property reads out of matrixRow.ts (a.<key>, e.<key>) instead of the unused constants.

important.name: unrefute --fix does not reopen an id a fixer bubbled before the refute
important.summary: apply_unrefute('fix') appends NOT_RESOLVED and drops the id from bubbles, and its docstring (and the pr_review.py docstring: 'so the next waves plans it') promise that Phase 5 waves see it open. That fails for an id a fixer bubbled before the developer refuted it, a path refute allows, since a bubble adds no closing status. Sequence: a fixer bubbles I3 (fixes/<fixer>.json keeps the bubble), the developer runs `refute I3`, then `unrefute I3 --fix`. On the next `waves`, wave_inputs -> _follow_up adds counted_bubbles(reports, parts) to `done`, so I3 is never planned (pr_review.py:1711). On the next `closeout`, apply_closeout replays every fixer report (closeout_review loads all of fixes/), and _apply_bubbles sees I3 as not closed. reopened_bubble_entry then appends BUBBLED and re-adds I3 to bubbles and bubble_up (review_merge.py:960-980). This silently turns the developer's --fix overrule back into a bubble.
fix: Have _follow_up / counted_bubbles leave out ids whose latest status is NOT_RESOLVED, and have _apply_bubbles skip a fixer bubble for an id whose latest resolution is NOT_RESOLVED and is dated after the bubble's wave. One way to decide that: compare against the resolution index of the id's REFUTED entry, or record the waves that came before the overrule in the NOT_RESOLVED entry.
Refuse `refute` for an id a planned fixer has already bubbled (counted_bubbles over the run's fix reports), naming `bubble`/`closeout --closed` as the route instead, so the sequence cannot arise.

important.name: fold-in-review drops a verified claim as a duplicate of an issue that is closed REFUTED
important.summary:
Section 3b Deduplicate says that after build a claim an existing issue already states is skipped and its id named, and Section 5 reports it as `duplicate of <id>`. Since this PR, an existing issue can be closed as REFUTED (by an -a build or by `refute`): it gets no fixer and counts closed in the verdict. A developer note that restates it, and that the 3b verification confirms in the tree, is then dropped as a duplicate, and the report line does not say the id is refuted. The developer reads `duplicate of I3`, assumes the defect is queued, and the verified defect ships. The new -a bullet at lines 149-152 covers only the opposite direction (refuting a folded issue), not a fold that contradicts a refutation.

Also (docs): fold-in-review SKILL.md:149-152 says that under -a 'the verification in section 3b is their only check'. A GitHub review fold is verified under section 3a's 'Verify first' (lines 76-81) and only goes through 3b when comments need splitting, so a URL fold has no 3b check at all. The same bullet says a fold's findings 'count as upheld at merge', while a post-build fold never goes through merge (it is appended to the built review directly, line 145).

Also (skill_package): The added bullet says a fold's findings get no check besides 'the verification in section 3b'. But a GitHub URL fold whose comments all hold is verified in section 3a ('Verify first') and folded by URL without passing through 3b. The bullet also says the developer can `refute` a folded issue 'once Phase 4 has passed'. Phase 4 has two runs, and `refute` needs only the first run (pr-review SKILL.md:55, Rule 6: `pre_fix_time` not pending), not the second-run pass.
fix: In Section 3b Deduplicate, add: when the matching issue's latest status is REFUTED and the claim verifies, do not skip it silently; report `matches refuted <id> (<refuter evidence>)` and offer the developer `unrefute <id> --fix` (or `--bubble`) per pr-review Phase 5 Rule 6. Add that reason to the Section 5 dropped-item reasons.
Alternatively, fold the verified claim under a new source id when its match is REFUTED, so it becomes an open issue with a fixer, and name the refuted id in its summary.
Reword to: 'the verification in section 3a or 3b is their only check', and 'count as upheld (at merge before build; a post-build fold is appended unrefuted)'.
Reword to: `the verification in sections 3a and 3b is their only check, and the developer can still refute a folded issue after build (once the Phase 4 first run has passed)`.

important.name: Phase 3 trigger names the Workflow call's own return, which SPK-1 showed is only the launch ack
important.summary: pr-review SKILL.md:262-263 (and review-local SKILL.md:102-103) say Phase 3 starts once the Workflow result has arrived, '(its return, or its completion notification)'. SPK-1 (docs/RESEARCH/pr-review/1016_workflow_spike.md:73-81) confirmed the Workflow call returns at once with 'Workflow launched in background. Task ID: ...' and the result arrives only as the later task-notification. Read literally, the immediate return satisfies the trigger, so a session can run `merge` while the workflow is still running. `merge` then refuses for missing refutations or reports, and the recovery prose (SKILL.md:268-276, and the missing-report rule in Phase 3 Step 1) tells the session to re-dispatch those entries as plain Agent calls, which races the still-running workflow agents and records duplicate reports. The script's result is the `{id, returned}` list (adversarial-review.js:64-72), which only the completion notification carries.
fix: Replace '(its return, or its completion notification)' with '(its completion notification; the call itself returns at once with a task id, which is not the result)' in pr-review SKILL.md:262-263 and review-local SKILL.md:102-103, and make the Temporal gate at pr-review SKILL.md:424-425 name the completion notification the same way.

important.name: Lone latest BUBBLED rule untested in Python and its TS mirror unpinned
important.summary: id_handling.all_issues_dispositioned (id_handling.py:83-98) drops an id whose latest resolution is BUBBLED from the resolution channel, so it counts only through bubbles/bubble_up; this decides whether the Layer 3 hook clears the Phase 5 sentinel. No Python test covers it: test_schema_hook_refuted.py pairs every BUBBLED entry with a bubble_up entry (lines 168-181), and the NOT_RESOLVED cases cover only the reopen rule. Removing "BUBBLED" from the status filter at id_handling.py:96 would let a review whose id was never bubbled clear the sentinel, and no Python test would fail. The TS port in bubbles.ts (BUBBLE_ONLY_STATUSES, REOPENED_STATUS at lines 58-59) has a behavioral test (bubbles.test.ts 'a latest BUBBLED counts only through bubbles or bubble_up'), but test_closed_status_mirror.py pins only CLOSING_STATUSES / STAMPING, so the two sides can drift apart without failing a test.
fix: Add a Layer 3 case to tests/hooks/test_schema_hook_refuted.py: I1 REFUTED, M1 REFUTED then BUBBLED, empty bubbles and bubble_up, a READY verdict; assert the sentinel stays armed. Keep the existing paired case as the positive control.

Expose the bubble-only statuses as a constant in id_handling (for example BUBBLE_ONLY_STATUSES = ("BUBBLED", REOPENED_STATUS)), use it at line 96, and extend tests/mods/test_closed_status_mirror.py to read bubbles.ts BUBBLE_ONLY_STATUSES and compare it with that constant.

fix: _incoherent docstring: 'REFUTED, BUBBLED and NOT_RESOLVED entries are exempt (build writes REFUTED entries before Phase 4)'. _closeout_reason docstring: 'a REFUTED entry dispositions its id through all_issues_dispositioned, a latest BUBBLED counts only through bubbles / bubble_up, a latest NOT_RESOLVED never counts; none of the three counts as a resolution or as SHA evidence'.

minor.summary:
The adversarial_check description says build 'adds counts and refuted_ids', but review_adversarial.complete_check (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/review_adversarial.py:320-321) also writes an empty unrefuted_ids and replaces result. The result example 'OK (2 checked, 1 refuted)' matches neither string the code emits: capture writes 'PENDING (<n> code refuters, <m> findings refuters)' (review_adversarial.py:308) and build writes 'OK (<n> checked, <m> refuted, <k> code findings)'. The schemas README (Section 1, verification_log shape contract) already states the accurate sequence, so the schema text is the one out of step.

Also (config): counts.findings_checked / findings_refuted / findings_upheld / code_findings have no descriptions. complete_check's docstring (review_adversarial.py:315-316) stresses that checked and refuted count refuter verdict entries, a different unit from refuted_ids (issue ids), so findings_refuted need not equal len(refuted_ids); a reader of the schema alone would assume they match. findings_upheld is also derived (checked - refuted), which the schema does not say.

Also (overall): The result example reads 'OK (2 checked, 1 refuted)' while review_adversarial.complete_check writes 'OK (N checked, M refuted, K code findings)' and capture writes 'PENDING (C code refuters, F findings refuters)'. The entry description says build adds counts and refuted_ids, but complete_check also writes unrefuted_ids: [] (as schemas/README.md correctly states).

Also (system_shape): PR_REVIEW.schema.json:318 says 'build adds counts and refuted_ids', but review_adversarial.complete_check (review_adversarial.py:311-321) also writes `unrefuted_ids: []` and replaces `result`. The `result` example at :352, 'OK (2 checked, 1 refuted)', is a shape the code never produces: build writes 'OK (<n> checked, <m> refuted, <k> code findings)' and capture writes 'PENDING (<c> code refuters, <f> findings refuters)' (review_adversarial.py:308). The schemas README (verification_log contract) describes the build step correctly, so the schema is the one that drifted.
fix: Line 318: change to 'Capture writes applies, workflow, code_slots, refute_slots and a PENDING result; build adds counts, refuted_ids and an empty unrefuted_ids and rewrites result as OK (...); refute and unrefute update refuted_ids and unrefuted_ids only, counts and result keep the build-time figures.'
Line 352: change the example to "'PENDING (1 code refuters, 2 findings refuters)' at capture, 'OK (2 checked, 1 refuted, 0 code findings)' after build".

Add a description to each counts property: findings_checked = 'verdict entries across the findings refuters' reports'; findings_refuted = 'refuted verdict entries (not issue ids; may differ from len(refuted_ids))'; findings_upheld = 'findings_checked - findings_refuted'; code_findings = 'findings across the code refuters' reports'.

Change the result description to the two real forms ('PENDING (<C> code refuters, <F> findings refuters)' at capture, 'OK (<N> checked, <M> refuted, <K> code findings)' at build) and make the entry description say build adds counts, refuted_ids and an empty unrefuted_ids.

Schema :318: 'build adds counts, refuted_ids and an empty unrefuted_ids and sets result'; :352: give both real forms, e.g. 'PENDING (2 code refuters, 5 findings refuters)' at capture, 'OK (12 checked, 3 refuted, 4 code findings)' after build.

minor.name: agent_usage top-level description omits the refuter roles
minor.summary: The role description now lists refuter / code_refuter for a pr-review -a refuter dispatched as an Agent call, and identify.ts claims those dispatches for the pr-review run (REFUTER_ROLES, identify.ts:46). The schema's top-level description still lists the run-owned roles as '(reviewer, fixer, orchestrator, planner, closer)' and calls any other dispatch a generic row, so it reads as if a refuter row were generic.
fix: Line 5: change '(reviewer, fixer, orchestrator, planner, closer)' to '(reviewer, fixer, orchestrator, planner, closer, and a pr-review -a refuter or code_refuter)'.

minor.name: Matrix tokens description contradicts the new workflow rows
minor.summary: tokens says rows the agent-watcher writes ('notes' starting 'agent-watcher auto row') sum tokens over every model request. The new workflow rows also start their notes with 'agent-watcher auto row' (matrixRow.ts:148) but hold tokens 0 because the slot is unobserved, as the dispatch_shape description at line 64 says. A rollup that trusts the tokens contract by the notes prefix averages those zeros in as measured cost.
fix: Line 68: append 'except `workflow` rows (dispatch_shape `workflow`, notes naming `unobserved: workflow agent`), which hold 0 because the slot is not observed'.

minor.name: closeout --deferred / --closed silently skip a REFUTED id
minor.summary: _cmd_closeout refuses only --resolved ids whose latest status is REFUTED (pr_review.py:2154-2158). --deferred and --closed on such an id reach _apply_deferred / _apply_closed, which treat REFUTED as already closed (CLOSED_STATUSES) and append nothing with no problem line: a developer-confirmed defer of a refuted id loses its RESOLVED defer entry and its needs_follow_up bubble_up entry silently. The spec's 'A silent skip' anti-goal names only bubble and --resolved, but the same dropped-decision case applies here.
fix: Extend the refusal in _cmd_closeout to the --deferred (and --closed) ids in ra.refuted_now(doc), with the same refuted_problem text naming unrefute, before anything is written.
Or have _apply_deferred return a problem for an id whose latest status is REFUTED instead of skipping it.

minor.name: fold-in-review README not updated for -a runs
minor.summary: SKILL.md gained the rule that folded findings are never refuted in an -a run and count as upheld at merge, and operating_rules.md gained the same rule. The skill's developer-facing README.md, which lists the 'Rules worth knowing', mentions neither -a, refutation, nor the developer's `refute` overrule for a folded issue. The review-local README this PR adds states 'Folded findings are never refuted', so the fold skill's own README is the one place that omits it.
fix: Add a bullet to README.md 'Rules worth knowing': `In an -a run, folded findings are not refuted: they count as upheld at merge, and the skill's own verification is their only check; the developer can refute a folded issue after build.`

minor.name: Model floor gains a one-row Agent/Model table that covers only refuters
minor.summary: The added table under 'Model floor (reviewer dispatch)' has one row, `refuter (-a only) | opus, from its args entry`, placed after prose that gives the reviewer models (opus, sonnet for a one-file bucket slot, never haiku). An `Agent | Model` table reads as the complete model map, yet it leaves out the reviewer slots, and it does not say whether 'refuter' means code refuters, findings refuters or both. The review-local README says both run opus.
fix: Replace the table with one sentence: `Every refuter of an -a run (code and findings refuters) runs opus, from its args entry.`
Or complete the table with the reviewer rows (opus default, sonnet for a one-file path-bucket slot), and name the row 'code and findings refuters (-a only)'.

minor.name: Prompt and brief contract still describes only reviewer prompts with AGENT_ROLE: reviewer
minor.summary: The 'Prompt and brief contract' section says each dispatch prompt is the four header lines with `AGENT_ROLE: reviewer`, and that every reviewer and fixer prompt gains the `Developer guidance:` line. Under -a the Workflow args carry refuter prompts with `AGENT_ROLE: code_refuter` or `AGENT_ROLE: refuter` (review_briefs.py:306-307), and the reviewer and refuter prompts get guidance from the Workflow script through args.guidance, not as a dispatched line. The skill's intro (lines 16-17) states the guidance exception, but the contract section itself was not updated, so the two parts of the skill disagree.
fix: Add one sentence after the prompt block: `Under -a, code refuter and findings refuter prompts carry AGENT_ROLE: code_refuter / refuter with their own briefs, and the Workflow script appends the guidance line (Phase 2, Under -a).`

minor.name: Workflow lists deliberately skipped repeat refuters as failures to recover
minor.summary:
Line 57 logs refute entries that repeat a target as 'not run', but row() flags only orphans. So `failed` (line 69) includes the repeats (returned false, no orphan flag), and line 71 tells the session to 'recover with a plain Agent dispatch' for agents the script chose not to run.

Also (overall): adversarial-review.js logs refute entries repeating a target as 'not run' (:53-57), but row() only flags orphans, so a repeat comes back {returned: false} without a flag, lands in `failed`, and the final log tells the session to 'recover with a plain Agent dispatch' (:69-71); the pr-review SKILL recovery rule excludes only orphan entries, so the session would run the entry the script just declared not run. capture never emits repeats today, so this is latent.
fix: Track repeats in a Set like orphans, mark their rows `repeat: true`, and exclude them from `failed` (`!r.returned && !r.orphan && !r.repeat`).
Collect the repeats in a Set and mark them in row() like orphans (e.g. `repeat: true`), excluding them from `failed`; add the flag to the SKILL's result description.

minor.name: Coherent-case hook test also passes on the hook's silent exit-0 paths
minor.summary: test_pending_review_with_overrule_entries_is_coherent asserts only returncode 0 and no 'INCOHERENCE'. validate_pr_json_schema.py also returns 0 without running Layer 2 on a schema setup error (_schema_check line 207-209) and when the target is not recognized as a review (_validate_target lines 292-297). A regression into either path would leave the test green. The sibling incoherent tests show the path is recognized today but do not protect this case.
fix: Also assert 'setup error' not in result.stderr. Or, since a coherent NOT READY review with no armed sentinel writes nothing, assert result.stderr == ''.

minor.name: Hand-rolled try/except/else in place of pytest.raises
minor.summary: test_a_project_lens_may_not_take_the_adv_prefix catches ValueError, copies the message and sets an empty string in the else branch so the final 'name in message' assert fails. pytest.raises(ValueError, match=re.escape(name)) does the same in one line, and its failure message says that nothing raised.
fix: Replace lines 388-394 with: with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=re.escape(name)): rp._check_project_lens(lens)

minor.name: Schema version hard-coded where sibling tests use SCHEMA_VERSION
minor.summary: TestReviewDocument asserts doc["version"] == "2.3.0". In the same PR, test_review_edit.py switched its literal to rmg.SCHEMA_VERSION, and test_pr_review_schema_adversarial.py already pins SCHEMA_VERSION against the schema's $version. The literal adds no protection and breaks on the next schema bump.
fix: Replace "2.3.0" with rmg.SCHEMA_VERSION at tests/lib/test_review_merge.py:406.

minor.name: Mixed-group merge_adversarial test duplicated in test_review_merge.py
minor.summary: TestMergeAdversarialMixedGroup.test_refuted_finding_leaves_only_its_evidence builds the same scenario as test_review_merge_adversarial.py::test_merge_adversarial_mixed_group_takes_its_shape_from_upheld_findings (lines 204-216): a refuted runtime finding and an upheld overall finding on one file merge into a single issue shaped by the upheld one, and the notes carry the refuted evidence. The PR adds a dedicated adversarial merge module, but this copy lives in the general merge tests. Its stricter full-dict assert (no 'also', no refuted severity) is the only part the other test lacks.
fix: Move the full-dict equality assert into test_merge_adversarial_mixed_group_takes_its_shape_from_upheld_findings (give the refuted finding an 'also' entry there) and delete TestMergeAdversarialMixedGroup from test_review_merge.py, dropping the now-unused Refutation, RefutationReport, finding_key and report_digest imports.

minor.name: 'only new closed status' test cannot catch another new status
minor.summary: test_refuted_is_the_only_new_closed_status checks that REFUTED is in CLOSED_STATUSES and that BUBBLED and NOT_RESOLVED are not. A different status added to CLOSED_STATUSES would still pass, so the name claims more than the asserts check. test_closed_status_mirror.py compares the TS arrays with CLOSED_STATUSES but does not pin CLOSED_STATUSES itself.
fix: Add assert set(rmg.CLOSED_STATUSES) == {"RESOLVED", "CLOSED_NO_ACTION", "REFUTED"} to the test (it can replace the three membership asserts).

minor.name: Test pins _named_ids, which has no production caller
minor.summary: test_not_resolved_latest_status_is_no_disposition asserts on rmg._named_ids (lines 113 and 115). This PR moved its only callers (review_edit._disposed_ids and the orphan check) to _mentioned_ids, and its docstring at review_merge.py:438-443 now says 'No production caller'. The test is that function's only user, so it keeps dead code alive and points readers at a disposition rule no shipped path applies. The same test's undispositioned_ids and compute_verdict asserts (lines 116-119) already cover the live behavior.
fix: Delete the two rmg._named_ids asserts (lines 113-115) and keep the undispositioned_ids and compute_verdict asserts; delete the dead _named_ids from review_merge.py:438-443.
If _named_ids is meant to stay, give it a production caller, and keep the asserts only once it has one.

minor.name: Mirror docstring overstates the 'either side' failure
minor.summary: The module docstring says the test 'fails when either side changes without the other'. The checks are one-way: test_the_keys_read_are_keys_workflow_args_writes asserts the keys the mod reads are a subset of the keys workflow_args writes, and test_every_slot_entry_carries_the_slot_keys does the same per entry. A key the library adds, which the mod never reads, passes. The subset rule is the right contract, but the docstring describes a stronger one.
fix: Reword line 8 to: 'This test fails when the mod reads a role, group or key the library no longer writes.'
